:::{#sol-cross-entropy-entropy}

1.
   $$
   \ba
   H(p, p)
   &= -\tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{1}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} \\
   &= \tfrac{1}{2} \cd 1 + \tfrac{1}{4} \cd 2 + \tfrac{1}{4} \cd 2 \\
   &= \tfrac{3}{2}.
   \ea
   $$

2. The range of $X$ is $\set{1, 2, 3}$, and $\P(X = k) = p_k$, so

   $$
   \ba
   \entropyf{X}
   &= -\sum_{k \in \rangef{X}} \P(X = k) \log_2 \P(X = k) \\
   &= -\tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{1}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} \\
   &= \tfrac{3}{2}.
   \ea
   $$

   This equals $H(p, p)$, because the two sums have the same terms.

3. By [the expectation form of cross-entropy](#thm-cross-entropy-expectation) with $q = p$,
   $H(p, p) = \E{-\log p_X}$.
   Since $\P(X = k) = p_k$, we have $-\log p_X = \surprisalf{X}$, the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of $X$.
   This is finite with probability 1, because $X$ takes only values with $p_k > 0$.
   So $H(p, p) = \E{\surprisalf{X}} = \entropyf{X}$ by the definition of entropy.

:::
